key_insight: Crystallographic {111} walls give single-crystal, atomically smooth vertical Si sheets without DRIE or EUV. They could serve as a low-Dit channel option for vertical-channel 4F2 transistors.
killer_doubt: KOH (110):(111) selectivity of ~100-400 erodes walls by 2h/R: a 3 um etch removes 15-60 nm, the entire 20-40 nm wall. No capacitor or tier isolation; potassium is CMOS-hostile.
decisive_experiment: Pattern oxide-masked <112> lines on (110) wafers and etch 2-3 um deep in K-free TMAH. Use TEM to map wall taper and roughness, then measure Dit and 85 C off-current on gated wall FETs. ~$80k.
prior_art: (110) KOH vertical-wall MEMS (1970s on); TMAH-etched {111} FinFET fins; Samsung/SK hynix VCT and Si/SiGe 3D DRAM already give crystalline channels (training knowledge).

key_insight: Cell-only wafers with sense amps and decoders in the accelerator's logic make the cell die ~100% array and push interface energy toward ~0.3 pJ/bit. Fits N-41's carrier slot naturally.
killer_doubt: One bond per column per 512 cells needs ~0.7 um pitch, so wafer-to-wafer only: logic and cell yields multiply (0.6x0.85=0.51), and one layer caps near 45 GB.
decisive_experiment: Join I-04714's experiment. W2W-bond a 28 nm logic MPW (SAs, sub-array decoders, repair) at 0.7-1 um to an IGZO or MIM cell wafer. Measure sense margin, bond yield and retention at 95-105 C. ~$600k.
prior_art: US10340261/US10600772: cell chip bonded to logic chip holding SAs and word drivers; US11996389 logic-on-DRAM-cell bond (via search snippet); UniIC SeDRAM; Phase B N-41.

key_insight: Sampling the bitline before and after charge sharing cancels offset, 1/f noise and precharge kTC together, a ~3-10 mV floor. Best as a logic-process sense amp under bonded cells.
killer_doubt: Offset-cancelling SAs already ship. Data-dependent BL-BL and WL coupling arise during sharing, which CDS cannot cancel. A 0.5 fF cell on a 13 fA leakage tail needs ~10 ms refresh.
decisive_experiment: Add a CDS arm to the N-04/I-11588 28-65 nm MPW. Use emulated 30 fF bitlines with 0.2-2 fF MIM cells and measure BER versus Cs under checkerboard and all-0 patterns at 85 C. ~+$50k.
prior_art: Samsung/SK hynix offset-cancellation sense amps (OCSA) in production; CIS CDS readout; Phase B N-04 charge-transfer pre-sense; advanced I-11588 neutralised bitline (training knowledge).

key_insight: The project needs a parametric 3D-tier cost and yield model internally anyway. Publishing it with a gain-cell eDRAM generator would cheaply seed university array design and U.S. talent.
killer_doubt: SKY130/GF180 have no DRAM capacitor. A 130 nm gain cell is ~1.5-3 um2, ~2,000x a 1b 6F2 bit (~0.0009 um2), so it trains circuit designers, not cell physics.
decisive_experiment: Release the tier cost/yield model and a gain-cell macro generator, then count outside tape-outs and citing groups within 12 months (~$150k). Proceed only if at least five outside groups tape out.
prior_art: OpenRAM SRAM compiler (UCSC/OSU); SKY130 and GF180 open PDKs; academic gain-cell eDRAM macros; R23's open sense-amp IP idea I-05632 was dropped (training knowledge).

key_insight: Under a 4x price spike, giving retired modules a second life over CXL adds real supply. Pooling also recovers stranded capacity without new fabs.
killer_doubt: Pond (ASPLOS 2023) estimated only ~7-9% DRAM savings from pooling, not 20-40%. Hyperscalers and CXL vendors already run pooling and DDR4 reuse (training knowledge).
decisive_experiment: Desk study (~$30k): from public Azure and Alibaba cluster traces, compute the stranded DRAM recoverable by 8-16-socket pools and the second-life module supply. Continue only if net bits exceed 15% after CXL latency limits.
prior_art: Microsoft Pond and GreenSKU DDR4 reuse via CXL; Meta TPP; Astera Labs, Samsung CMM-B, Liqid, UnifabriX pooling; in-study I-06854 and I-01312 (training knowledge).

key_insight: Redox sites store charge at a fixed potential, offering in principle multi-level plateaus and charge independent of dielectric thickness, aimed squarely at the capacitor charge wall.
killer_doubt: With no counter-ions, an electron hopping from electrode to cluster stays on one plate: terminal charge remains C_dielectric x V. Ionic compensation makes a pseudocapacitor: ~1e5 cycles versus 1e12+.
decisive_experiment: Graft Keggin POMs on TiN and cap with 5 nm ZrO2 and TiN. Measure charge versus frequency (1 kHz-100 MHz) and after 1e9 cycles. Stop if charge does not beat the bare MIM at 10 MHz. ~$100k.
prior_art: ZettaCore porphyrin memory (Lindsey/Bocian); Busche et al., Nature 2014, polyoxometalate flash cells (Glasgow); Phase B N-17 alive-speculative; N-25's pseudocapacitive variant failed on endurance.

key_insight: If roll-to-roll memory foil (I-01819) works, U.S. converter sites, web-handling staff and tolling contracts could add capacity fastest, with no EUV, quartz crucibles or helium.
killer_doubt: Converter halls run at ISO 8-9, 1,000-10,000x ISO 5 particle counts. NIL, spatial ALD, inspection and enclosures are all new capex, so retrofitting saves perhaps 10-20% of line cost (estimate).
decisive_experiment: Fold into I-01819. After its 100 nm imprint result, build a $50k teardown cost model of one converter line: reusable tools, enclosure cost, and particle counts measured on a running web after an ISO 6 retrofit.
prior_art: PragmatIC FlexIC fabs; HP Labs SAIL roll-to-roll TFTs; Applied Materials and Buhler vacuum web coaters; in-study advanced I-01819 (training knowledge).

key_insight: Vacuum web coaters lay down multilayers at ~100x lower cost per m2. Decoupling the tier stack from the wafer would make tiers a laminated commodity film.
killer_doubt: Web-coated oxide barriers show ~1e2-1e3 pinholes/cm2 (estimate), while each of 127 interlayers needs <1e-3/cm2 for short-free tiers. Stack deposition is perhaps 10-20% of 3D wafer cost.
decisive_experiment: Coat a 16-pair Mo/SiOx stack on stainless or polyimide web in a pilot coater and laminate it onto 200 mm wafers. Map interlayer shorts per cm2 and voids by acoustic microscopy. Stop above 0.01 shorts/cm2. ~$150k.
prior_art: Vacuum web coaters for optical and barrier multilayers (Applied Materials SmartWeb, Buhler Leybold); 3M co-extruded multilayer optical film; 3D NAND PECVD tier stacks (training knowledge).

key_insight: Self-rolling strained bilayers fold a patterned film into a compact multi-turn volume with one release mask. That helps only where footprint near logic, not cost, is the constraint.
killer_doubt: Rolling relocates film rather than multiplying it: a 20-turn roll uses 20x the processed wafer area, so cost/bit is unchanged. Inner-turn contacts and TFT bending strain add loss.
decisive_experiment: Spreadsheet first (~$5k): $/GB of rolled versus flat film from the same process. Only if footprint matters, roll a 64x64 IGZO TFT array on a strained SiNx bilayer and measure Vt shift and contact yield. ~$150k.
prior_art: O. G. Schmidt group (IFW Dresden, TU Chemnitz): rolled-up nanomembrane capacitors, inductors and micro-batteries; R27's laminated-sheet I-07806 dropped on the same cost logic (training knowledge).

key_insight: Counting electrons rather than volts is the right instinct. Electron resolution helps only at a tiny node, so the gain belongs to in-cell or per-segment gain, not the bitline foot.
killer_doubt: At the foot the cell shares charge with the bitline; kTC on 10 fF is ~40 e- rms, so 10-electron resolution is moot. Sub-3 nm islands drift with background charge.
decisive_experiment: Paper check (~$10k): noise budget for a 0.2 fF cell on a 5-20 fF vertical bitline, SET versus CDS or charge-transfer amp. Only if the SET wins, fabricate 100 PADOX SETs and map offset-charge spread at 300-360 K.
prior_art: NTT PADOX silicon SETs (Takahashi, 1990s); Hitachi room-temperature single-electron memory (Yano, 1994) and PLEDM; Phase B N-04 and in-study I-01381 (training knowledge).

key_insight: LLM traffic is mostly predictable: weights stream in fixed order and KV caches are append-then-scan. A just-in-time placement controller lets us-latency shift strings (CCD, racetrack) serve it.
killer_doubt: A 64-bit string at imec's ~6 MHz takes ~10 us per rotation; averaging under 40 ns needs misses below ~0.2%. Data-dependent top-k attention and batch churn may break that.
decisive_experiment: Trace-driven simulator (~$80k): replay vLLM/SGLang decode and training traces against a parameterized shift-string memory (length, clock, ports). Report the fraction of bytes served within 40 ns versus clock rate. This sets I-10793's clock target.
prior_art: IBM 650 SOAP (1950s); ShiftsReduce, TU Dresden, ACM TACO 2019, shift-minimizing racetrack placement (via search snippet); SanDisk/SK hynix HBF serves weights at flash latency.

key_insight: Epitaxial band-offset wells store charge with no capacitor and no tunnel oxide in the write path, one of triage's endurance-safe routes: a semiconductor channel.
killer_doubt: 64 ms at 85 C needs ~0.78 eV (1e12/s attempt rate). Ge-rich wells give ~0.3-0.5 eV after confinement: ns-10 us retention. A 128-cell series string reads in us, not ns.
decisive_experiment: Grow a 10-period Si/Si0.5Ge0.5 superlattice, etch gated pillars and write holes by GIDL. Measure Vt-decay retention from 25-125 C to extract an Arrhenius barrier. Stop if Ea < 0.7 eV. ~$150k.
prior_art: Ertosun and Saraswat SiGe quantum-well 1T-DRAM (Stanford, EDL 2008); Z-RAM floating-body DRAM; NEO 3D X-DRAM; Samsung/SK hynix Si/SiGe 3D DRAM stacks (training knowledge).
